about: The two per-tool memory stores, pinned as layout plus golden post-write state (D4). WP6 adopts this rather than re-deciding it. Both are machine-global, both are written only through their write_status.py subcommand, and both are read back at research time to fill {{STANDING_NOTES}}. test_items.py drives add-watch-item into a temporary XDG_STATE_HOME and asserts equality against after_one_write; the add-method-note subcommand is specified here and lands with the write_status pass, which extends that test to drive it the same way.

cask:cursor-cli.note: User wants any change to cursor-agent's shell hook or `agent record` behavior called out.

brew:attention.topic: where attention's real config-path changes are announced
brew:attention.note: attention moves its config path in ordinary commits and mentions it nowhere in the release body. Read the `config` package's diff across the range rather than the CHANGELOG.

keying: Both are keyed by tool id ({source}:{name}), one array per tool, appended to. A tool id always contains a colon, so any future reserved key WP6 wants for the third (global) store cannot collide with one.
not_pinned_here: The global method-note store. It is filled by promotion during convergence (schemas.md §1.7b), convergence does not exist yet, and nothing in this pass writes it. WP6 owns it.
